input.note: The claim credits "improved operating efficiency" as the primary driver of operating income growth rather than revenue growth alone. The filing does not report "improved operating efficiency" as a specific quantified figure. However, the passages mention efficiency gains qualitatively (e.g., "efficiency gains across the Microsoft Cloud" in E1, E2). The filing shows that operating income increased 21% (from $128,528M to $155,237M) while revenue increased 18% (from $281,724M to $331,839M). Operating expenses increased only 7% (from $65,365M to $70,228M), and cost of revenue increased 21% (from $87,831M to $106,374M). The components that contribute to operating income are revenue, cost of revenue, and operating expenses, which are reported as separate line items.
